answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by binding reputation to a bonded signing key. Each member locks collateral and signs every deal with one quill, a key whose history is tracked on a shared ledger. Clones need a fresh bond each and must earn trust through real trades; reusing a quill merges them into one and burns the stake. A wallet no bigger than a walnut cannot buy a trusted army. Audits of conflicting signatures are as hard as karst, so duplicates get caught. The attacker pays per fake while the network pays little, making Sybils a losing trade.
